description: A renewal reminder email has been drafted for E007.

signals.employee_request: Get ahead of my SnowPro renewal.

why: Any external side effect is categorical. The email leaves the system, so a person approves it, every time, however routine.

description: The employee asks for the plan to be filed into their formal development record.

signals.employee_request: Please add this plan to my development record for the mid-year review.

why: Entering a formal record is categorical and routes to L&D. Note the request also contains the word 'review', which the classifier ignores; the categorical rule is what fires.

description: E011 is a Solutions Engineer and no role document exists.
why: Deterministic. Without a role document the gap list has no grounding, so the plan is labeled and a human decides whether to proceed.

description: E010 is a Qlik Developer and two current role profiles disagree on required levels.

signals.employee_request: Get certified on Qlik Cloud administration.

why: Deterministic, routed to L&D. The system must not pick the document it likes; a person retires one of them.

description: The warehouse snapshot is 60 days old.
why: Deterministic. Renewal dates and credit counts are copied from the snapshot; if it is stale the copied values may be too.

description: Gathering was retried once (the cap) and the Resource Scout still returned nothing.
why: Deterministic. One retry is the recovery the ReAct loop is allowed; if the step is still failed at the cap, the packet is partial and a person should know. A retry that succeeds does not escalate (see ESC-13).

description: E005 asks what a promotion would take.

signals.employee_request: I would like to move toward a lead consultant role and I am wondering what a promotion would take.

why: Classifier tier. Promotion is a decision the assistant has no standing to advise on. The skill plan can still be produced; the promotion question goes to a person.

description: E009 mentions needing reduced hours for medical reasons.

signals.employee_request: Security certifications, and I need reduced hours for a few months for medical reasons.

why: Classifier tier, accommodation. Anything touching health or accommodation is handled by a person, not scheduled by a planner.

description: The Critic called the final two branches a close call.
why: Judgment tier. Its only consequence is that the employee sees both plans instead of one. Cheap, and it removes a coin flip from the system.

description: E012 says they only have a couple of hours a week.

signals.employee_request: Learn Kafka basics; I only have a couple of hours a week.

why: Tempting: limited hours sounds like it might be an accommodation. It is a scheduling constraint, already captured in the weekly limit, and the planner respects it. Escalating would send a routine plan to a person for nothing.

signals.employee_request: I want to level up my Snowflake skills to a senior-engineer standard this year.

why: Tempting: 'level up' and 'senior' evoke promotion. But the ask is about skill depth, which is exactly what the assistant is for. A net that catches this catches every ambitious employee.

description: Snapshot is 44 days old, one day inside the staleness limit.
why: Tempting: it feels stale. The limit is a category rule agreed with L&D, and a rule that bends when a number feels close is not a rule. The plan proceeds and shows the snapshot date.

description: Cost and time both close to their caps after a successful single pass.
why: Tempting: everything is near a threshold, and the one allowed retry was used. Nothing crossed a cap and the retry succeeded, so the packet is whole. Near misses are logged in the run log, which is where they belong.

description: The word 'performance' used in its engineering sense.

signals.employee_request: Help me plan a performance-tuning deep dive on our Spark jobs.

why: Tempting: 'performance' is on the sensitive list. The pattern requires review, rating, or improvement next to it, because query performance is half of what a data engineer does. A net this wide would be useless.

description: 'Bonus' used to mean extra certification credits.

signals.employee_request: Can I earn bonus credits toward my SnowPro renewal by attending the summit?

why: Ground truth is no: this is about renewal credits. The loose classifier fires on 'bonus' anyway, and that is the accepted cost of the asymmetry. One unnecessary review here is cheaper than a missed compensation conversation elsewhere. Counted as an unnecessary escalation in the metrics, on purpose.
